2025-11-20T17:27:42.5777291Z     def resolve_name(name):
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5777383Z         """
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5777467Z         Resolve a name to an object.
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5777529Z     
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5777691Z         It is expected that `name` will be a string in one of the following
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5777870Z         formats, where W is shorthand for a valid Python identifier and dot stands
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5777981Z         for a literal period in these pseudo-regexes:
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5778055Z     
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5778118Z         W(.W)*
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5778193Z         W(.W)*:(W(.W)*)?
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5778261Z

2025-11-20T17:27:42.5778612Z         some part of the dotted name is a package, and the rest is an object
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5778783Z         somewhere within that package, possibly nested inside other objects.
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5778967Z         Because the place where the package stops and the object hierarchy starts
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5779145Z         can't be inferred by inspection, repeated attempts to import must be done

2025-11-20T17:27:42.5779280Z

2025-11-20T17:27:42.5779626Z         provision of a single colon: the dotted name to the left of the colon is a
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5779929Z         package to be imported, and the dotted name to the right is the object
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5780104Z         hierarchy within that package. Only one import is needed in this form. If
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5780242Z         it ends with the colon, then a module object is returned.
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5780309Z     
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5780484Z         The function will return an object (which might be a module), or raise one
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5780570Z         of the following exceptions:
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5780637Z

2025-11-20T17:27:42.5781257Z                          within the imported package to get to the desired object.

2025-11-20T17:27:42.5782630Z         gd = m.groupdict()
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5782710Z         if gd.get('cln'):
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5782851Z             # there is a colon - a one-step import is all that's needed

2025-11-20T17:27:42.5783150Z             parts = parts.split('.') if parts else []
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5783225Z         else:

2025-11-20T17:27:42.5862658Z     def resolve_name(name):
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5862734Z         """
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5862819Z         Resolve a name to an object.
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5862880Z     
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5863046Z         It is expected that `name` will be a string in one of the following
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5863230Z         formats, where W is shorthand for a valid Python identifier and dot stands
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5863345Z         for a literal period in these pseudo-regexes:
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5863414Z     
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5863481Z         W(.W)*
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5863554Z         W(.W)*:(W(.W)*)?
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5863816Z     
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5864007Z         The first form is intended for backward compatibility only. It assumes that
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5864171Z         some part of the dotted name is a package, and the rest is an object
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5864664Z         somewhere within that package, possibly nested inside other objects.
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5864852Z         Because the place where the package stops and the object hierarchy starts
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5865031Z         can't be inferred by inspection, repeated attempts to import must be done
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5865109Z         with this form.
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5865169Z     
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5865335Z         In the second form, the caller makes the division point clear through the
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5865513Z         provision of a single colon: the dotted name to the left of the colon is a
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5865677Z         package to be imported, and the dotted name to the right is the object
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5865850Z         hierarchy within that package. Only one import is needed in this form. If
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5865989Z         it ends with the colon, then a module object is returned.
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5866049Z     
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5866237Z         The function will return an object (which might be a module), or raise one
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5866324Z         of the following exceptions:
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5866383Z     
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5866632Z         ValueError - if `name` isn't in a recognised format
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5866771Z         ImportError - if an import failed when it shouldn't have
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5866958Z         AttributeError - if a failure occurred when traversing the object hierarchy
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5867106Z                          within the imported package to get to the desired object.
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5867172Z         """
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5867260Z         global _NAME_PATTERN
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5867342Z         if _NAME_PATTERN is None:
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5867454Z             # Lazy import to speedup Python startup time
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5867532Z             import re
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5867634Z             dotted_words = r'(?!\d)(\w+)(\.(?!\d)(\w+))*'
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5867762Z             _NAME_PATTERN = re.compile(f'^(?P<pkg>{dotted_words})'
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5867880Z                                        f'(?P<cln>:(?P<obj>{dotted_words})?)?$',
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5867967Z                                        re.UNICODE)
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868039Z     
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868127Z         m = _NAME_PATTERN.match(name)
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868192Z         if not m:
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868303Z             raise ValueError(f'invalid format: {name!r}')
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868378Z         gd = m.groupdict()
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868453Z         if gd.get('cln'):
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868595Z             # there is a colon - a one-step import is all that's needed
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868698Z             mod = importlib.import_module(gd['pkg'])
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868778Z             parts = gd.get('obj')
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868888Z             parts = parts.split('.') if parts else []
2025-11-20T17:27:42.5868953Z         else:
